title: Every TV screen has a word on the phone's status line
body:
## Summary
TV_WORDS was a Partial record, so the worked lesson and the Workroom showed their raw ids on the phone.

## Description
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:35 `Partial<Record<Session["screen"], string>>`; desk/src/lib/session/store.ts:35 Screen has 40 ids, the list had 38. The phone printed "TV · worked" and "The TV is on workroom". A hand-maintained list checked by nothing (SKILL 4.7). Fixed: Record<Screen, string>, so a new screen is a tsc error at the list.

## Flow
- Open a worked lesson (or Adult mode's Workroom) on the TV
- Before: the phone's header says "TV · worked"
- After: "TV · a worked lesson" / "the Workroom"

## Expected impact
The phone always names the TV's screen in words. Could break: nothing; type-only plus two strings.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the list is checked against the Screen union
Before: 2 of 40 screens without words; seeded red: tsc TS2739 missing worked, workroom
After: 0 of 40; tsc green
Method: gate - tsc --noEmit with the Record type
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:35 (before) Partial<Record<...>>
tsc: missing the following properties from type 'Record<Screen, string>': worked, workroom

title: Check it on the TV fails the way its siblings do
body:
## Summary
The Say panel's checkSentence had no catch and discarded the route's error: a dropped call left "sending…" and an unhandled rejection; a refusal read "failed".

## Description
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:305 (before) `try { ... setMsg(r.ok ? "on the TV" : "failed") } finally {...}`; the other 11 network handlers catch and say "That did not reach the desk." and show j.error. /api/analyse answers 409 NOBODY_AT_DESK for an english sentence with no one seated (desk/src/app/api/analyse/route.ts:31). Registry: async-ui-states / failure-states.

## Flow
- Wi-Fi drops, press Check it on the TV
- Before: "sending…" stays, unhandled rejection
- After: "That did not reach the desk."; a 409 shows the route's line

## Expected impact
The learner knows to retry or to seat someone. Could break: nothing; the ok path is unchanged.

## Evaluation
Claim: resilience - one failure contract across the phone handlers
Before: 11 of 12 handlers catch; checkSentence threw (SW1 red)
After: 12 of 12 (SW1 green)
Method: gate - SW1 runs the handler slice against a rejected call, 409, 500 and ok
Result: better
Gate: none

title: A camera granted after the panel let it go is stopped
body:
## Summary
The camera effect set any stream getUserMedia returned, even one granted after the panel stopped wanting it, and stopped nothing on unmount.

## Description
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:140-144 (before) had no liveness guard and no cleanup; the TV's Pair QR effect (desk/src/tv/screens.tsx:60) carries the `live` pattern. A tab picked while the browser's permission prompt was open left the camera on with no panel asking. Policy-tighten: the camera runs only while a panel wants it. Registry: media-playback / media-resource-lifecycle.

## Flow
- Open Capture, leave the permission prompt open, pick another tab, then allow
- Before: the late stream becomes cam and keeps running
- After: stopped on arrival; the stream in use is stopped when the page goes

## Expected impact
No camera light on a panel that never asked. Could break: nothing in the wanted path (control in SW2).

## Evaluation
Claim: other - privacy: camera on only while asked
Before: late grant: 0 of 1 tracks stopped, stream set as cam (SW2 red)
After: stopped at once, never set; wanted stream set and stopped on unmount (SW2 green)
Method: gate - SW2 runs the effect slice with a gated getUserMedia
Result: better
Gate: policy-tighten
evidence:
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:142 (before) .then((st) => { setCam(st); ... })
desk/src/tv/screens.tsx:60 let live = true ... if (live) setSvg(x)
tools/phone-panel-test.cjs SW2

title: The phone-sized rule holds on every panel, not only typed answers
body:
## Summary
Case 13's rule (44 px targets, 16 px fields) held for the typed answers only; the other fields zoomed iOS at 15 px and the tab bar, presets, samples and role switch were 26-37 px tall.

## Description
tools/phone-panel-test.cjs:299 states the rule and checks .pask input and .proute button. desk/src/app/globals.css: .field controls inherited .phone's 15 px (join code, name, Point & ask, Say it, plan slot, paragraph, second go, Add an assignment), .ppaper-find 15 px; .pnav button ~37 px, .presets button ~27 px, .samples button ~30 px, .ptop .who button ~26 px, .field controls ~42 px. The file is listed under tv-surface; it styles the phone.

## Flow
- Tap the join code field on an iPhone
- Before: Safari zooms in; the tabs are under 44 px
- After: 16 px fields, 44 px targets

## Expected impact
No zoom jump on every field; tabs and chips hit reliably. Could break: a taller tab bar and chips (visual check owed at 390 px).

## Evaluation
Claim: user - phone fields and targets meet the stated rule
Before: 2 of 4 field rules >= 16 px; 0 of 5 target rules >= 44 px (SW3, SW4 red)
After: 4 of 4; 5 of 5 (SW3, SW4 green)
Method: gate - SW3/SW4 read the comment-stripped stylesheet
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
tools/phone-panel-test.cjs:299 'the tap targets are at least 44 px, and ... 16 px'
desk/src/app/globals.css:23 .phone font-size 15px; :55 .field controls (no font-size); :29 .pnav button padding 12px 2px, font 11px

body:
## Summary The one status line every phone handler writes to (.pstatus) was a plain div, never announced. ## Description desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:712 (before) `
{msg}
`; the Essay panel's notes carry role="alert" (2 sites, :652, :675). Registry: accessibility / live-region-architecture. Fixed: role="status" aria-live="polite". ## Flow - VoiceOver on, send a page with Wi-Fi down - Before: "That did not reach the desk." is drawn, not spoken - After: spoken politely ## Expected impact Outcomes reach a learner using a screen reader. Could break: nothing visual. ## Evaluation Claim: user - outcomes announced Before: 0 of 1 status line is a live region (SW11 red) After: 1 of 1 (SW11 green) Method: gate - SW11 reads the comment-stripped page Result: better Gate: none

title: The new learner's name is posted per keystroke and can land out of order
body:
## Summary
The Profile name field posts profile.draft on every keystroke without waiting, so a slower earlier post can overwrite the last one and Save keeps a prefix.

## Description
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:490 onChange posts {patch:{name}} un-awaited per key; a browser runs up to 6 requests in parallel and the server applies them in arrival order (last write wins). The phone's input then shows "Ema" while the draft holds "Em" (pname resyncs only on a draft id change, :131), and Save (:491) saves the draft. Fix: serialise the posts (a promise chain) or send the name once on Save/blur.

## Flow
- Type a name quickly on a busy LAN
- An earlier keystroke's post arrives last
- The TV shows, and Save keeps, the shorter name

## Expected impact
The saved learner has the name typed. Could break: the TV's live name echo if posts are batched.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - the saved name is the typed name
Before: N un-awaited posts per name of N letters, unordered (code read)
After: 1 ordered write (predicted)
Method: simulation - needs a harness that delays responses out of order
Result: better
Gate: none
evidence:
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:490 onChange={(e) => { setPname(...); post({ type: "profile.draft", patch: { name: e.target.value } }); }}
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:131 pname resyncs on draft id only
instrument: slice harness of the Profile onChange with a post stub that resolves the second-to-last call last, against a store stub applying in arrival order: final draft name equals the input

Claim: user - phone fields 16 px
Before: 7 Linga phone controls at 15 px (code read)
After: 0 (predicted)

Result: better

title: End session can be pressed twice before it shows busy
body:
## Summary
endSession sets busy only after session.end returns, so a second tap within that round trip posts session.end and /api/memory twice.

## Description
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:438-440 awaits post({type:"session.end"}) then setBusy(true); the button is disabled={busy} (:680). tools/tv-recap-test.cjs:337 M4 pins "busy covers only the memory call", so the fix changes a pinned contract: busy (or a ref guard) from the first tap. /api/memory answers already:true on a repeat, so the cost is a duplicate end and a duplicate write attempt.

## Flow
- Tap End session twice quickly
- Two session.end posts, two /api/memory calls
- Fix: guard from the first tap and restate M4

## Expected impact
One end per tap burst. Could break: M4's wording; the busy label shows during session.end too.

## Evaluation
Claim: quality - one end per press
Before: 2 taps in the round trip -> 2 session.end (code read)
After: 1 (predicted)
Method: simulation - in-tree contract (M4) without a verifier for the double tap
Result: better
Gate: contract
evidence:
desk/src/app/phone/page.tsx:439-440
tools/tv-recap-test.cjs:337 'busy covers only the memory call'
instrument: slice harness of endSession with a gated post: call twice before resolving, count session.end posts (2 today, 1 after); restate M4 in the same commit
